newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: INTERVIEW - Manila rate cuts follow domestic trend.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Manila rate cuts follow domestic trend.

text.p: The cut in the Philippine Central Bank's overnight rates on Wednesday was in line with the trend in domestic interest rates, Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said on Wednesday.
He told Reuters in a telephone interview that the adjustment in rates was made despite a 0.25 percentage point increase in U.S. interest rates on Tuesday.
"We do not necessarily follow U.S. interest rates. In fact, our overnight rate is higher than the 91-day T-bill rate," he said. He declined to offer a forecast on interest rate direction.

The Central Bank on Wednesday lowered its overnight borrowing rate to 9.9 from 10.0 percent. Its move to cut that rate was made after a continued decline in the benchmark 91-day T-bill rate to single digit levels for two consecutive weeks.

The 91-day rate slipped to 9.724 percent on Monday in the weekly auction from a previous 9.804 percent. Bankers had said the decline in domestic interest rates stemmed from prevailing low inflation and high liquidity in the market.
Singson said the Central Bank had not changed its monetary policy when it allowed a further lowering of its interest rate. "It (our policy) has always been prudent and flexible," he said.
"We are comfortable as long as there is no peso speculation," he added, referring to the impact of lower domestic interest rates on the Philippine currency.
Asked if there was any peso speculation, Singson declined comment.

The peso weakened to 26.37 in early morning trade following the rate cuts. Traders attributed the decline to the higher U.S. federal funds rate as well as the Central Bank's lowering of its overnight borrowing rates.
Earlier on Wednesday, the Central Bank also trimmed its overnight lending rate to 12.65 percent from 12.75 percent.
